Colours to avoid

  • Raspberry Ice#9F3753Too clear for Soft Summer — reads as bright summer pink
  • Periwinkle#CCCCFFToo clear and too violet — our periwinkle is far paler
  • Orchid#DA70D6Too clear and too magenta
  • Soft Fuchsia#FF99FFThe clearest colour on any sister palette
  • Muted Gold#D2B450This is mustard wearing a soft name
  • Khaki Green#8A865DToo olive — the yellow has to go
  • Olive Moss#A2AF7BToo olive
  • Faded Coral#E0A994Coolable, but only below the waist
  • Copper Rose#996666Coolable, but only below the waist
  • Ballet Rose#D3ADB1Too light and too clear — this is a Light Summer colour
  • Powder Blue#B0E0E6Too light — our powder blue is half the clarity
  • Sea Glass#DEE2DFToo light and too clear
  • True Black#000000Too deep and too stark — no true black in this palette
  • Bright White#FFFFFFToo stark; even soft white is greyed
  • Jet Black#0E0E10Black with nothing in it — our charcoal is blue-tinged
  • Camel#C19A6BThe classic camel — too warm and too deep here
  • Warm Beige#D8BCABCream with a yellow cast; greige is the cool version
  • Mustard#FFDB58Gold at full strength — mushroom gold is the muted one
  • Sun Yellow#FFE87CUngreyed warm gold — dune is as close as this gets
  • Tomato Red#FF6347Orange-leaning red — dusty raspberry is the version that works
  • Neon Coral#FF6044The warmest colour here — dusty rose instead
  • Bright Fuchsia#FF5BFCClearer than soft fuchsia, which was already the limit
  • Electric Blue#7DF9FFPure, clear blue — grey it toward smoky blue
  • Pumpkin#FF7518Hot and clear — clay rose is the muted one
  • Rust#B7410EDeep and hot — dusty peach is the version that works
  • Emerald Green#5FBB9CToo clear for a green — eucalyptus is the version that works
  • Auburn#A52A2AWarm red-brown — dusty rose is the cool one
  • Copper#B87333Metallic orange — nowhere in this palette
